business_problem: Migu Video needed to replace slowing relational systems with a distributed database architecture that could handle event-driven viewing surges, complex aggregation queries, and rapid feature evolution for a massive sports-streaming audience.
solution_summary: Migu Video modernized its core media platform by progressively migrating from traditional relational databases to MongoDB Enterprise Advanced and MongoDB Ops Manager. MongoDB became the backbone for the company's video operation system, which supports content production, marketing, auditing, royalties, KPI statistics, and interactive features such as bullet-screen comments. The document model let engineers handle unstructured and fast-changing video-service data without repeatedly redesigning schemas, while the distributed architecture scaled as MongoDB deployments grew to more than 450 instances across core systems. Migu also uses zone sharding to segment users by area code so regional sub-centers can keep traffic close to viewers while a main center retains global visibility. Ops Manager automates deployment, monitoring, and backup, allowing the team to expand public-cloud and edge-computing capabilities without adding equivalent operational headcount.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Powers Migu Video's distributed operational data layer for streaming, content, and interactive-media workloads.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Ops Manager
solution_components.role: Automates database deployment, monitoring, backup, and operational management across Migu's large instance estate.

data_flow: Streaming, programming, interaction, and operations data enters MongoDB Enterprise Advanced across distributed regional and central deployments; zone sharding keeps user data close to each area, while Ops Manager manages deployment and observability as the platform serves live events and background aggregation workloads.
business_outcome: Migu Video improved core-system performance dramatically, sustained Olympics-scale peaks with zero failures, and gave product teams a more flexible foundation for immersive video experiences and new interactive features.
